nodes.description: Public string state variable holding the quiz question text.
Address state variable storing the owner/game master who started the game.
Bytes32 state variable holding the keccak256 hash of the expected answer; gates the payout logic.
Public payable function that initializes responseHash, question and questionSender when the game is not yet started.
External payable function that verifies the answer and transfers the whole contract balance to msg.sender.
Public payable function restricted to questionSender that drains the contract balance to the caller.
Public payable function restricted to questionSender that updates question and responseHash.
Payable fallback function that accepts plain ether transfers without further logic.
Caller-controlled address used for ownership checks, recipient of transfers and stored as questionSender.
Transaction origin used in the Play require check, enabling phishing-style authentication bypass.
msg.sender.transfer(this.balance) inside Play; external value call executed before state is fully settled, reentrancy-prone.
msg.sender.transfer(this.balance) inside StopGame; external value call to an arbitrary caller address.
String parameter of StartGame that becomes the stored question.
String parameter of StartGame hashed with keccak256 into responseHash.
String parameter of Play hashed and compared against responseHash to authorise payout.
String parameter of NewQuestion that overwrites the stored question.
Bytes32 parameter of NewQuestion that overwrites responseHash.

edges.reason: StartGame writes the keccak256 hash of _response into responseHash.
StartGame stores the supplied question string into the question state variable.
StartGame assigns the caller-controlled msg.sender to questionSender, making the first caller the privileged owner.
The _response parameter is hashed and written to responseHash inside StartGame.
The _question parameter flows into StartGame body to set the stored question.
The _response parameter is consumed by StartGame for hashing.
Play reads responseHash to compare it against keccak256(_response).
Play hashes the _response parameter and compares it with responseHash.
The _response parameter is used inside Play's answer verification.
Play requires msg.sender == tx.origin, a tx.origin based authentication check that can be bypassed via phishing.
Play compares msg.sender with tx.origin, controlling whether execution proceeds.
Play performs an external value transfer of the full balance to msg.sender when the answer matches.
The transfer in Play sends this.balance to the caller-controlled msg.sender, which may re-enter.
StopGame requires msg.sender == questionSender, gating the drain to the owner.
questionSender is read by StopGame to authorise the caller.
StopGame transfers the whole contract balance to the caller after the ownership check.
The transfer in StopGame sends this.balance to msg.sender, an externally controlled address.
NewQuestion requires msg.sender == questionSender before mutating game state.
questionSender is read by NewQuestion to authenticate the caller.
NewQuestion overwrites the question state variable with the new question.
NewQuestion overwrites responseHash with the caller-supplied bytes32.
The _question parameter is consumed by NewQuestion to update the question.
The _responseHash parameter is consumed by NewQuestion to update responseHash.
The _responseHash parameter directly overwrites the responseHash state variable.
The payable fallback lets an attacker contract accept and react to ether transfers during Play's payout.
The payable fallback lets a malicious recipient receive funds during StopGame's payout.

normalization_plan.reason: Parameter only feeds the question state write inside StartGame and has no independent identity.
Parameter is hashed into responseHash exclusively within StartGame.
Parameter is used only by Play's answer-hash comparison and payout gate.
Parameter is consumed solely by NewQuestion when updating the question.
Parameter is consumed solely by NewQuestion when overwriting responseHash.
